newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN GENERAL NEWS - DEC 10.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN GENERAL NEWS - DEC 10.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Under proposed changes to the universal service obligation (USO), which stipulates that a basic standard of telecommunications service must be available to all subscribers, all Australians will have access to digital data services such as the Internet and e-mail by 2000. Page 1.

While Prime Minister John Howard yesterday reaffirmed a strong commitment by the Government and the Australian people to human rights through a Parliament motion on International Human Rights Day, Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer was the only Coalition Mnister to sign a Labor and Democrat sponsored Federal Parliamentarians' Code of Race Ethics designed to mark the day. Page 2.

Keen to capitalise on the Coalition's continued high standing in the opinion polls, Prime Minister John Howard will celebrate nine months as the leader of Parliament with a major state of the nation address describing the achievements of the Coalition and its priorities for the coming year. Page 3.

A program has been launched by the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (ASIO) to measure the threat posed to Australian industry by an increasing global trend towards economic espionage. The annual report tabled by ASIO says the organisation was aware of foreign agents being sent to Australia to steal economic information to help advance their own industries. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In an interview with New South Wales Police Royal Commission investigators only hours before his suicide on November 4, 67-year-old former Supreme Court judge David Yeldham admitted he was bisexual and said he was deeply ashamed of his homosexual encountes at railway stations and was fearful of arrest and blackmail. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday dismissed controversial Independent MP Pauline Hanson's argument for clamping down on foreign investment as nothing more than a simplistic notion, saying it was easy for Hanson to go around Australia "touching sensitive chords". Page 1.

After reaping almost A$14 billion from the previous sale of electricity businesses, the Victorian Government plans to generate more than A$10 billion by selling the State's gas industry and its remaining publicly owned electricity assets in a move which culd cut Victoria's A$20 billion debt in half. Page 1.

A new Monash University study, the first to single out the impact of the Austudy changes on university students, says the number of university students affected by changes to Austudy eligibility rules will be double that predicted by the Howard Governmentand could be as many as 60,000. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In its second submission to the Wallis inquiry into the financial system, lodged yesterday, the Insurance and Superannuation Commission revealed half Australia's superannuation funds had significant weaknesses, five per cent were in serious trouble and the problems were likely to escalate if prudential safeguards were reduced. Page 1.

The New South Wales Police Royal Commission yesterday released parts of two interviews held with former Supreme Court Judge David Yeldham, one held at his own request, with investigators on the morning of his suicide. In the interviews, Yeldham admitted to being bisexual but denied being a paedophile, saying he would never have sexual contact with someone under the age of 18. Page 1.

Seventeen years after the stop-start Eastern Suburbs rail line was opened to the public, the New South Wales Government has called for private sector support for a A$120 million, three-kilometre extension of the line to Bondi Beach. Expressions of interes will be called next month for private developers to design and construct the extension. Page 1.

The New South Wales Government has agreed to give St Vincent's Hospital, which State Health Minister Andrew Refshauge planned to relocate to St George Hospital at Kogarah earlier this year, A$80 million to renovate and rebuild on its present Darlinghurst site. Page 3.
THE AGE

After yesterday's decision to sell-off the former Gas and Fuel Corporation and the remainder of the electricity industry, Victoria is expected to regain its triple-A credit rating and halve its A$20 billion debt. Experts are predicting the Government wil make A$5 billion from the sale of the Gas and Fuel Corporation, and another A$5 billion from other electricity assets. Page A1.

A bribery hearing for the first policeman charged under Operation Bart, held before the Melbourne Magistrate's Court yesterday, was told Victorian policemen were offered inducements by window shutter operators including things such as beer, money, interstte holidays and football tickets. Page A1.

A letter addressed to Small Business Victoria chief executive Chris Siddons calling for a donation to the Labor Party caused embarrassment yesterday when it ended up on the desk of a State Government department head. The Labor Party's state secretary Joh Lenders admitted in the letter the Party had a long way to go before being re-elected. Page A1.

Former VicRoads executive Dr Max Lay yesterday complimented Bicycle Victoria's plan for the construction of a comprehensive cycling network on Melbourne's roads, saying it was practical and feasible. Lay said that while 500 kilometres of off-road paths had been built, not enough road space had been set aside for cyclists. Page A3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
